So verdicts follow the 2026-10-22-c skill and baseline grades and the standards they keep: a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or the finding's stated fix addresses it; a silent fix, or a mention only under assumptions, notes or behaviour changes, does not count. Match every expected shape and let unexp.evidence: Finding 6 (lines 27-29) reports input line 33 `_ -> {:error, :insert_failed}` and finding 8 (lines 35-37) the identical errors ("Three different failures (bad input, underage, duplicate) all return `{:error, :invalid}`"); the `with` chains (lines 97-102, 106-115) pass errors through, and `string_field/2` matches each shape (lines 120-122).

Convert external strings to atoms with e.evidence: Finding 1 (lines 7-9); lines 126-128 `defp parse_role("admin"), do: {:ok, :admin}` / `defp parse_role("member"), do: {:ok, :member}` / `defp parse_role(other), do: {:error, {:unknown_role, other}}`.

Branch with function clauses and guards.evidence: Finding 9 (lines 39-41) reports the nesting ("`import_user/2` nests `try`, `if`, `if`, `case`, and `if`") with a flat `with` as the fix; the improved code is flat and line 99 is a one-line `if`.

Return `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reaso.evidence: Finding 1 (line 8) "It also raises on a missing role", finding 2 (lines 11-13) the `rescue _ ->` and `String.to_integer/1`; the improved code has no `rescue` and parses with line 131 `case Integer.parse(text) do`.

Use `and`, `or`, `not` when the operands.evidence: Finding 4 (lines 19-21) reports input line 21 `is_binary(email) && age >= 18` (its line 27 half is recorded as a false positive); the improved code has no `&&` or `!`.

Give each function one return shape.evidence: Finding 5 (lines 23-25) reports `return_id`; `import_user/2` always returns `{:ok, user}` (line 101) or a step's error.

Comments explain why; documentation goes.evidence: Finding 13 (lines 55-56) covers the comments and keeps the line 11 reason (kept at line 111); finding 14 (lines 58-59) "`120` and `18` become `@max_age` and `@min_age`"; lines 76-77 `@min_age 18` / `@max_age 120`; `@moduledoc` at line 70 and `@doc` at lines 79-92.

Keep functions short and at one level of.evidence: Finding 9 (lines 39-41) reports the nesting; `import_user/2` (lines 94-103) is a two-step `with` over `parse_params/1` and `insert_user/1`.

Write pipelines that start with a value.evidence: Input line 12 `email = params["email"] |> String.downcase()` (single-step pipe) is named by no finding: finding 15 (line 62) names `params["email"]` only as returning `nil`, finding 2 (line 12) `String.downcase(nil)` only as raising, and finding 12 (lines 51-53) only line 55. The improved code fixes it silently (line 112 `email = String.downcase(email)`).

Validate input with changesets.evidence: Finding 7 (lines 31-33) reports the input line 24 lookup as a race and the unvalidated struct, with `unique_constraint(:email)` as the fix; lines 139-143 insert through `User.changeset/2`, whose sketch ends in line 164 `|> unique_constraint(:email)`, with `role` set on the struct before `cast/3` (line 140); the `Repo.get_by/2` lookup is gone.

Send processes only the data they need.evidence: Finding 10 (line 44) "The closure also captures and copies the whole `user` struct" with "build the email first" as the fix; lines 146-148 `email = welcome_email(user)` / `Task.Supervisor.start_child(Accounts.TaskSupervisor, fn -> Mailer.deliver(email) end)`.
